_readme: The client's config for the scripts in tools/ghl. Copy this file to clients/<CLIENT_SLUG>/config.json (clients/ is never committed), then replace every placeholder in angle brackets. client: the business name. locationId: the sub-account id, the part after /location/ in the GHL address. tokenFile: the NAME of the file in ~/.secrets that holds the sub-account's Private Integration token, never the token itself. calendarOwnerUserId: the GHL user id of <PLACEHOLDER_USER>, who owns the calendar and every task until the client has a GHL user (survey.js lists the users and their ids). Keys that start with _ are notes: the scripts ignore them. Full guide: tools/ghl/README.md.

instantly._readme: Only if the client runs cold email in Instantly; otherwise delete this whole block. webhookUrl is the Inbound Webhook URL of the workflow 'Instantly - Interested Partner Reply': copy it from that workflow's trigger. fire-test.js posts its test lead there and refuses a URL of another location.

structure._readme: This client's changes to the standard structure (spec/structure.json). A field or pipeline with a standard name replaces the standard one, a new name adds one, and a 'remove' block drops names (tools/ghl/README.md has the rules). Always client-specific: the Partner Type options (from the blueprint, ending with Other), the segment/ tags (lower case, one per partner group, ending with segment/other), and the calendar slug and description. build-structure.js refuses to run while any of them is missing or still a placeholder.

calendar._readme: These keys replace the standard calendar's. The standard: 20 minutes, Monday and Tuesday 10:00 to 17:00 in the account's time zone, owned by calendarOwnerUserId. Add slotDuration or openHours here only if the client wants other times.
calendar.description: A 20-minute intro call with a prospective referral partner for the <PROGRAM_NAME>.

ids._readme: Filled by: node tools/ghl/survey.js --client <CLIENT_SLUG> --ids. Paste its output over this whole block once the structure, forms and workflows exist (run it again after each). double-check.js compares these ids with the account; enroll.js and move-stage.js read them; the flowcharts read them too.
